baton-rouge.TITLE: Baton Rouge HOA Management — Local Team, Local Office — CMGT
baton-rouge.META_DESCRIPTION: HOA management in Baton Rouge from the team headquartered here. 4.2★ across 535 reviews and named Baton Rouge's #1 property management company in 2026.
baton-rouge.GBP_NAME: CMGT - Association, Condo, and Rental Management
baton-rouge.HERO_LEDE: CMGT started with one Denham Springs community in 2007 and never left. Our office is on Aspen Square, our managers live in the parishes they serve, and when you call, someone who has driven your neighborhood picks up.
baton-rouge.AWARD_TEXT: #1 Best Property Management Company in Baton Rouge
baton-rouge.SINCE_LABEL: managing communities in this market ever since
baton-rouge.OFFICE_P: Plenty of management companies serve Baton Rouge from somewhere else. Ours is the office our team drives to — you are welcome to visit, though we ask that you call ahead so the right person is here for you.
baton-rouge.CONTACT_ROLE: Your Baton Rouge point of contact · CEO & Founder
baton-rouge.PARISH_PHRASE: East Baton Rouge, Livingston, and Ascension parishes
baton-rouge.VENDOR_COPY: Local vendor relationships built over eighteen years here, plus site visits so the board isn't the one chasing contractors.
baton-rouge.CARD6_P: A dedicated Insurance & Reserve department tracks coverage and reserve health year-round — critical in a parish where one storm reprices a master policy.
baton-rouge.COVER_SUB: Our Baton Rouge team manages communities throughout East Baton Rouge, Livingston, and Ascension parishes.
baton-rouge.COVERAGE_CHIPS: Baton RougeDenham SpringsPrairievilleGonzalesZacharyCentralWalker
baton-rouge.STORY_H: We didn't expand into Baton Rouge. We started here.
baton-rouge.STORY_P1: CMGT opened with a single community in Denham Springs in 2007 and grew across the capital region one referral at a time — no acquisitions, no private-equity money, no outside investors. When the 2016 flood put much of this area underwater, our own office was closed for four days, then we were back at work for the communities that needed us most. That's not a case study we bought. It happened to our neighbors, and to us.
baton-rouge.STORY_P2: Managing here has its own realities. Coverage and reserves move with every Gulf storm season, East Baton Rouge, Livingston, and Ascension each record and enforce a little differently, and homeowners expect a manager who already understands all of it. Because our managers live in these parishes, we're not learning your community when the storm is already in the Gulf — we know it before the first cone is drawn.
baton-rouge.FAQ1_A: Yes. Our office is at 140 Aspen Square Ste H in Denham Springs, and it has been our home since the company started in 2007. We're a Louisiana company with a Louisiana office — not a national brand with a satellite listing.
baton-rouge.FAQ2_A: We manage communities throughout East Baton Rouge, Livingston, and Ascension parishes — including Baton Rouge, Denham Springs, Prairieville, Gonzales, Zachary, Central, and Walker. Ask us for references in your specific area; we will happily connect you with a nearby board.
baton-rouge.FAQ3_Q: How does CMGT handle hurricane season here?
baton-rouge.FAQ3_A: Storm planning, vendor mobilization, and owner communication are in place before the season starts, and our Insurance & Reserve department monitors coverage year-round. See our hurricane preparedness guide for HOA communities.
baton-rouge.REL2_P: The board plan and homeowner communications that get a Gulf South community through a storm.

shreveport.TITLE: Shreveport HOA Management — North Louisiana — CMGT
shreveport.META_DESCRIPTION: HOA management in Shreveport and North Louisiana — a local office, a local team, and full-service management backed by nearly 400 communities.

shreveport.HERO_LEDE: Our office is downtown on Crockett Street — not four hours south. The manager assigned to your community lives up here, backed by the largest HOA management company in the state.
shreveport.SINCE_LABEL: independently owned and Louisiana-based ever since
shreveport.OFFICE_P: The most common thing we hear from North Louisiana boards is that management companies here are either tiny and stretched thin, or headquartered somewhere far away. We have an office downtown and people in this market, with the back-office depth of a statewide firm behind them.
shreveport.SERVICE_AREA_PHRASE: Shreveport, Bossier City, and North Louisiana
shreveport.CONTACT_ROLE: Your North Louisiana point of contact · CEO & Founder
shreveport.VENDOR_COPY: Bidding, oversight, and site visits handled by people in this market — so the board isn't calling contractors between jobs.
shreveport.CARD6_P: A dedicated Insurance & Reserve department tracks coverage and reserve health year-round, so renewals and reserve funding never arrive as a surprise at budget time.
shreveport.COVER_H: Shreveport, Bossier City, and up the I-20 corridor.
shreveport.COVER_SUB: North Louisiana is its own market, and we treat it that way — not as an outpost of the Gulf South.
shreveport.COVERAGE_CHIPS: ShreveportBossier CityMonroe
shreveport.STORY_H: North Louisiana is not south Louisiana. We don't manage it like it is.
shreveport.STORY_P1: CMGT started in Denham Springs in 2007 and grew across the state one referral at a time — no acquisitions, no outside investors. Growing that way taught us something useful: you cannot serve a market you don't live in. So we opened an office here rather than adding North Louisiana to somebody's driving route.
shreveport.STORY_P2: The concerns up here are genuinely different from the coast. Boards are weighing severe-weather and freeze exposure rather than hurricane season, and many communities have never had professional management at all — they have been run on paper letters and volunteer labor for years. We bring structure without making anyone feel behind for needing it.
shreveport.FAQ1_A: Yes. Our North Louisiana office is at 717 Crockett St Ste 2031 in downtown Shreveport, and the manager assigned to your community lives in this market. You will not be handed to someone driving up from Baton Rouge.
shreveport.FAQ2_A: We serve communities in Caddo, Bossier, and Ouachita parishes — Shreveport, Bossier City, and Monroe. We're actively growing here, so if your community is nearby and not on that list, ask us anyway.
shreveport.FAQ3_Q: You're a statewide company — will a North Louisiana community be a priority?
shreveport.FAQ3_A: Every community gets a dedicated manager and the same service standard, whether it's our 5th community or our 389th. The advantage of a statewide firm is the bench behind that manager: in-house accounting, insurance and reserves, covenants, and maintenance specialists that a small local operator simply cannot staff.

daphne.TITLE: Daphne HOA Management — Alabama Gulf Coast — CMGT
daphne.META_DESCRIPTION: HOA management in Daphne and across the Alabama Gulf Coast — a real Eastern Shore office, a local manager, and financials shared with every owner.
daphne.HERO_LEDE: Our office is on Equity Drive in Daphne — not across a state line. The manager assigned to your community lives on this side of the bay, backed by the largest HOA management company in the Gulf South.
daphne.OFFICE_PHOTO_HINT: Drop a map screenshot or exterior photo of the Equity Drive office
daphne.OFFICE_P: Baldwin County has grown fast enough that plenty of management companies now claim it from somewhere else. Our office is in Daphne and our people are in this market — you can put a face and an address to the company you hire.
daphne.SERVICE_AREA_PHRASE: Daphne, the Eastern Shore, and the Alabama Gulf Coast
daphne.CONTACT_ROLE: Your Alabama Gulf Coast point of contact · CEO & Founder
daphne.VENDOR_COPY: Our vendors on this coast are lined up and insurance-verified before the season starts, so a Baldwin County community is not competing for a tarp crew the week after a storm.
daphne.CARD6_P: Coverage reviewed continuously and reserves funded against real coastal replacement costs — so a claim or a special assessment is not the first time anyone looks.
daphne.COVER_H: Across the Eastern Shore and Baldwin County.
daphne.COVER_SUB: From Daphne and Fairhope down through Foley, and west across the bay to Mobile.
daphne.COVERAGE_CHIPS: DaphneFairhopeFoleySilverhillMobile
daphne.STORY_H: Coastal Alabama is its own insurance market.
daphne.STORY_P1: Boards here learn the vocabulary faster than most: wind-and-hail deductibles, named-storm exclusions, the difference between what the master policy covers and what an owner is left holding. Premiums on this coast have moved in one direction for years, and a board that treats insurance as an annual formality is the board that finds the gap mid-claim.
daphne.STORY_P2: We monitor association coverage year-round rather than at renewal — it is written into the management agreement — and we build the reserve plan around what replacement actually costs on the Gulf Coast today, not what it cost when the study was written.
daphne.FAQ1_A: Yes. Our Alabama Gulf Coast office is at 26241 Equity Dr. Ste. 101 in Daphne, and the manager on your community works from this market — not from Louisiana.
daphne.FAQ2_A: We manage single-family associations, townhome communities, and condominium associations across Daphne, Fairhope, Foley, Silverhill, and the Mobile area. We are happy to tell you which communities near you we already serve.
daphne.FAQ3_Q: How do you handle hurricane season on this coast?
daphne.FAQ3_A: The storm plan is built before June 1 — emergency vendors lined up and insurance-verified, master coverage reviewed for gaps, and a communication plan owners actually have in hand. When weather hits we mobilize, document damage for the claim, and manage the recovery through to rebuild.
daphne.REL2_P: The board plan and homeowner communications that get a Gulf Coast community through a storm.
